mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with falling housing starts (HOUST) indicates weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% interacts with a simultaneous decline in personal income (PAYEMS) to signal restrictive monetary policy coincident with weakening income growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real retail sales (RSAFS) above trend by more than 1.5% for three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the unemployment rate and a fall in payroll employment (UNRATE up and PAYEMS down) signals labor market softening, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% for five consecutive months signals a robust supply expansion, which boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
